title: Count the change
prompt:
A customer pays 2000 cents (20 dollars) for a repair that costs 1375 cents. The program already works out `change` in cents. Fill in `dollars` and `cents` so the last line prints the change as whole dollars and leftover cents.

When it works, `python3 change.py` prints `Change: 6 dollars and 25 cents`. The tests also try other prices.
hints: 625 cents is how many whole dollars? Which operator throws away the part after the decimal point?
`//` gives the whole dollars and `%` gives what is left over.
explain_after: `//` is floor division and `%` gives the remainder [py-046]. Together they split 625 into 6 hundreds with 25 left over. Keeping money in whole cents also keeps the numbers whole, which is why many shop programs do it.
